title: Software Engineering with Agents – there is a need for more humanity in SE and beyond
summary: Reflections after FSE in Montreal: more AI papers, fewer field studies. Benchmarks look impressive, but we still need empirical evidence from real teams and human judgment in the loop.

title: Summer 2026 – where are we going now?
summary: With AI writing more of the code, engineers can focus on design, specifications and guardrails. AI amplifies expertise rather than replacing it.

title: Levels of automated code development…
summary: A review of a taxonomy that grades AI code generation from L0 (token-level help) to L5 (full automation). A useful vocabulary for deciding who is responsible for what.

title: What are you talking about – one agent asked another…
summary: When two agents program together, high semantic-alignment scores can be a warning sign of agents echoing each other. A lesson in how a metric can mislead.

title: Can we force LLMs to generate the code we really want?
summary: Thirteen LLMs, one question: can feedback enforce design patterns? Simple iterative pass/fail feedback worked best, and functionality did not suffer.

title: My prompt is better than your prompt – how to optimize your prompts in the age of agentic AI
summary: Reinforcement learning with rewards shaped by unit-test results improves prompts beyond what manual prompt engineering achieves.

title: 15 years of Software Center – A Look in the Mirror and over the Front Windshield
summary: From agile and architecture, through DevOps and CI/CD, to ML and AI: how fifteen years of industry–academia work shifted what companies need to measure.

title: Junior Architects with Shaky Logic: Testing AI's Real-World Coding Skills – article review
summary: Three LLMs against 212 real production commits: success rates from 0 to 60%. Good at small routine functions, not to be trusted alone with critical code.

title: The Synthetic Engineer: Measuring the Real Impact of AI on Software Delivery
summary: A framework combining DORA metrics, AI usage and effect metrics (acceptance, rework, stability) and occasional developer surveys, and a warning about vanity metrics such as lines of code generated.

title: From Gutenberg to Google and on to AI
summary: Like compilers hid the hardware, LLMs hide programming details, opening software creation to product owners and requirements engineers.

title: How to improve the code reviews
summary: Reordering files in a review so the riskiest come first raises reviewer engagement and comment quality. Size metrics and LLMs can pick those files automatically.

title: Assessing the maturity of a metric team
summary: Three things make measurement programs last: a formal mandate, integration with product development, and a stable team over time.

title: Can we predict quality of service level quality based on metrics?
summary: Across 700+ web services, code and interface metrics correlate with response time, availability and throughput.

title: Your code and AI – more than precision and recall!
summary: AI tools for code quality should be judged by their effect on the product, not only by precision, recall and F1.

title: Actionable software metrics – an interesting new article
summary: A metric is actionable when it is practical, supports a decision and is fresh enough to matter. Metrics that apply across products trigger more action.

title: Succeeding with large scale measurement programs
summary: Measurement programs succeed when built around decisions: measurement systems, information quality and indicators that trigger action.
